metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Sub-graph Audit Checklist (Batch 8 - FINAL)
metadata.description: Final batch of checklist items for remaining sub-graph properties covering IC canisters, Stargate bridge, Nova folding, SelfCall pattern, native token handling, governance, and lzCompose callback.

checklist.title: Verify IC Canister Interaction Encrypts State with VetKey-Derived AES-GCM Keys
detection_procedure: 1. Locate the IC canister interaction code (likely in cli/ or client-common/)
2. Identify the VetKey derivation process via ACTION-IC-DERIVE-ENCRYPTION-KEY
3. Verify that AES-GCM authenticated encryption is used for state encryption
4. Check that plaintext state is NEVER sent to IC canisters without encryption
5. Verify encryption key derivation includes proper domain separation
6. Confirm nonces are unique per encryption operation (counter or random)
7. Check that decryption verifies authentication tag before returning plaintext
8. Verify error handling doesn't leak plaintext on decryption failures

executable_checks.assertion: AES-GCM encryption is used with VetKey-derived keys

executable_checks.command: Review state encryption flow for plaintext exposure
executable_checks.assertion: No plaintext state is transmitted to IC canisters
Nonces are properly generated and never reused

checklist.notes: IC canister storage is semi-trusted. Encryption is mandatory to protect user privacy. VetKey derivation ensures only authorized users can access encrypted state. Any plaintext exposure to canisters is a critical privacy violation.

checklist.title: Verify Stargate Bridge Enforces Slippage Protection and Handles Refunds
detection_procedure: 1. Locate the Stargate bridge integration (likely in contracts/ adaptor code)
2. Identify ACTION-SG-VALIDATE-SLIPPAGE and verify minAmountOut is properly calculated
3. Check that user-provided slippage tolerance is bounded (e.g., max 5%)
4. Verify quote fee (ACTION-SG-QUOTE-FEE) accounts for gas and protocol fees
5. Check that underlying token approval uses exact amount (not unlimited)
6. Verify refund mechanism (ACTION-SG-REFUND) handles STATE-SG-FAILED-SLIPPAGE
7. Confirm failed bridge attempts credit user on source chain
8. Check for front-running protection on slippage-sensitive operations

executable_checks.assertion: No arbitrary token/ETH transfers in bridge flow
Bridge reverts when output amount < minAmountOut
Slippage protection parameters are present in bridge calls

checklist.notes: Stargate bridge involves cross-chain value transfer. Slippage protection is critical as MEV bots can exploit price changes during bridge execution. Refund mechanism must work reliably for failed bridges.

checklist.title: Verify Nova IVC Folding Produces Valid Accumulators and Handles Witness Errors
detection_procedure: 1. Locate Nova folding implementation (likely in zkp/ or decider-prover/)
2. Verify accumulator update follows Nova IVC specification
3. Check that relaxed R1CS instances are correctly computed
4. Verify cross-term computation (T) is correct
5. Check random challenge (r) is generated from proper transcript
6. Verify local verification (ACTION-VERIFY-IVC-LOCAL) catches invalid witnesses
7. Confirm circuit satisfaction check rejects malformed witnesses
8. Check that folding preserves public inputs across steps

executable_checks.assertion: All Nova IVC tests pass

executable_checks.command: Review Nova accumulator update for correctness vs specification
executable_checks.assertion: Accumulator update follows Nova paper algorithm
Nova primitives are correctly referenced

checklist.notes: Nova IVC soundness is critical for the entire proof system. Invalid folding could allow forged proofs. Local verification step must catch any witness errors before the expensive Groth16 decider runs.

checklist.title: Verify SelfCall Pattern Prevents External Reentrancy via Dual-Condition Check
detection_procedure: 1. Locate the SelfCall pattern implementation (likely in contracts/)
2. Identify the onlySelfCall modifier
3. Verify modifier checks BOTH conditions: msg.sender == address(this) AND context flag
4. Check that context flag (ACTION-ENABLE-SELFCALL) is set only in controlled functions
5. Verify context flag is cleared (ACTION-DISABLE-SELFCALL) after protected call completes
6. Check for any paths where external caller could satisfy both conditions
7. Verify protected functions don't have alternative entry points
8. Confirm rejection state (STATE-SELFCALL-REJECTED) properly reverts

executable_checks.assertion: No reentrancy vulnerabilities in selfcall-protected functions
External callers are rejected by onlySelfCall modifier
SelfCall pattern is implemented with dual-condition check

checklist.notes: The SelfCall pattern is a reentrancy guard variant that allows controlled internal calls while blocking external reentrancy. Both msg.sender == address(this) AND the context flag must be checked - checking only msg.sender is insufficient as delegatecall can spoof this.

checklist.title: Verify Native ETH Handling with msg.value Validation and WETH Wrapping
detection_procedure: 1. Locate native ETH handling code (likely in LiquidityManager)
2. Verify msg.value validation occurs BEFORE any processing
3. Check that expected ETH amount is compared against msg.value
4. Verify WETH wrapping (ACTION-WRAP-ETH-TO-WETH) uses exact msg.value
5. Check excess ETH refund mechanism (ACTION-REFUND-EXCESS-ETH) returns to correct recipient
6. Verify no ETH can get stuck in contract after operations
7. Check receive() and fallback() functions don't accept arbitrary ETH
8. Confirm failed operations refund ETH to sender

executable_checks.assertion: No locked ETH or arbitrary ETH sends detected
Excess ETH is refunded to sender
Operations revert when msg.value doesn't match expected amount

checklist.notes: Native ETH requires special handling compared to ERC20. msg.value must be validated to prevent users losing funds. WETH wrapping must be atomic with the operation. Excess ETH must be refunded, not kept by contract.

checklist.title: Verify Admin Functions Restricted to Owner with Proper Access Control
detection_procedure: 1. Locate all governance/admin functions in contracts/
2. Verify each admin function has onlyOwner modifier
3. Check setFeeParams, withdrawRewards, setVerifiers, registerToken, updateToken, setMinter, upgradeContract
4. Verify owner cannot be set to zero address
5. Check two-step ownership transfer if implemented
6. Note: No timelock - verify this is intentional design decision
7. Verify proxy admin (if upgradeable) is properly secured
8. Check for any backdoor admin functions without modifiers

executable_checks.assertion: No missing zero checks or unprotected upgrades
Non-owner calls to admin functions revert
All admin functions use onlyOwner modifier

checklist.notes: WARNING: No timelock mentioned - admin actions take immediate effect. This is a centralization risk. Consider documenting or implementing timelock for critical operations like setVerifiers or upgradeContract. Owner compromise = full protocol compromise.

checklist.title: Verify lzCompose Callback Validates Caller and Stargate Origin
detection_procedure: 1. Locate the lzCompose callback implementation (likely in adaptor contracts)
2. Verify ACTION-VALIDATE-CALLER checks msg.sender == LayerZero endpoint address
3. Verify ACTION-VALIDATE-STARGATE-ORIGIN checks _from is in registered Stargate pool set
4. Check that both validations occur BEFORE any state changes or token processing
5. Verify compose message decoding (ACTION-DECODE-COMPOSE-MSG) handles malformed data
6. Check error handling doesn't leave partial state on failure
7. Verify STATE-COMPOSE-FAILED-STORED allows recovery/retry without re-execution
8. Check for replay protection on compose messages

executable_checks.assertion: No arbitrary sends or unchecked calls in lzCompose
lzCompose reverts when caller is not LayerZero endpoint
lzCompose reverts when _from is not registered Stargate pool

checklist.notes: lzCompose is a critical cross-chain entry point. Without proper validation, attackers could forge compose messages to steal funds. Both caller (LayerZero endpoint) AND origin (Stargate pool) must be validated. Failed composes must be stored for recovery, not lost.
